title: 1999 Miami Dolphins season
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of the 1999 Miami Dolphins season, the team's 34th campaign and 30th in the NFL, which marked quarterback Dan Marino's 17th and final season. The document covers the season overview, including Marino's mid-season injury against the New England Patriots, backup Damon Huard's 4–1 stint as starter, and the team's strong 7–1 first half followed by a 2–6 second-half decline, ultimately finishing 9–7 and clinching the AFC's final wild card spot via tiebreakers over the Kansas City Chiefs. The document is organized into sections covering the offseason (1999 NFL draft), team roster, regular season (including schedule, standings, and detailed week-by-week game summaries from Weeks 1 through 17), and the playoffs. The game summaries highlight key moments such as the season opener against the defending champion Denver Broncos, the comeback win at Indianapolis, Marino's injury game at New England, Huard's starts, Marino's disastrous five-interception return against Dallas on Thanksgiving Day, and Marino's final regular season win over San Diego. The playoff section details the Dolphins' 20–17 wild card upset of the Seattle Seahawks—Marino's final career win and the last game at the Kingdome—and their humiliating 62–7 divisional round loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the most lopsided playoff loss in the Super Bowl era, which served as the final games for both Marino and head coach Jimmy Johnson.
